the stress relaxation due scission in an elastomer operating at a constant deformation and temperature can be predicted from the stress relaxation due healing at a different temperature.
the stress relaxation in elastomers due to scission can be calculated from the stress relaxation in an elastomer that does not heal.
a simple correspondence principle can be used to predict the scission-induced stress relaxation in elastomeric materials that operate at a constant deformation while at an arbitrary temperature.

a new approach to the analysis of scission-induced stress relaxation.
the development of a method for estimating the lifetime and stress relaxation of elastomeric components.
the scission of elastomeric components, which can occur at elevated temperatures, due to the action of an external stress field.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a scission-induced stress relaxation in elastomeric materials can be predicted from a knowledge of the stress relaxation in the absence of scission, and a knowledge of the scission kinetics.

scission-induced stress relaxation in elastomeric materials at elevated temperatures can be predicted using the same methods that are currently applied to predict stress relaxation at room temperature.

scission-induced relaxation can be predicted for a given material at an elevated temperature if the material's relaxation behavior is known at a low temperature, and the scission rate is known at the high temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the stress relaxation in a scission-healing material at a given temperature is the same as that of an equivalent non-scission-healing material operating at the same deformation but at a higher temperature.
the stress relaxation due scission is a function of the deformation and the temperature, and that it is independent of the time scale over which the deformation is applied.
